purpose: Quizartinib is used to treat a type of blood cancer called acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in adults whose cancer has a specific gene mutation called FLT3-ITD. It is used together with chemotherapy to help fight the cancer or on its own after other treatments to help keep the cancer from coming back.
how_it_works: Your leukemia cells have an overactive protein called FLT3 that tells cancer cells to grow out of control. Quizartinib works like a 'lock blocker' — it attaches to that FLT3 protein and stops it from sending those growth signals. This helps slow down or stop the cancer cells from multiplying.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, feeling very tired, low blood counts (which can increase your risk of infection, bleeding, or anemia), loss of appetite, swelling in your hands or feet, shortness of breath, and changes in heart rhythm.
warnings: This medication can cause a serious heart rhythm problem called QT prolongation, which can be life-threatening. Your doctor will regularly check your heart with an EKG. Tell your doctor right away if you feel your heart racing, fluttering, or if you faint. It can also lower your blood cell counts significantly, so watch for signs of infection like fever, chills, or unusual bleeding. This medicine can harm an unborn baby, so reliable birth control is very important for both men and women during treatment.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 35.4 mg taken by mouth once daily, with or without food. Your doctor may adjust the dose depending on how you tolerate it and what other treatments you are receiving. Always take it at the same time each day and never skip or double a dose without checking with your care team first.
